Title: Students Educating Students
NewsSubTitle: SPIE students outreach to Dawood Public School
NewsSummary: SPIE conducted a CPR awareness camp at the Dawood Public School. The activity was attended by more than 150 students. The students were trained in groups to allow students to practice individually.
NewsContent:
SPIE (the interprofessional Society for Promoting Innovation in Education) conducted its second CPR awareness session at the Dawood Public School on April 13, 2019 under the leadership of 4th year MBBS student Muhammad Ali. This is part of an extensive on-going program of health education designed and delivered by students, quality assured by AKU faculty, and supported logistically by CIME. This activity was attended by 70 students from grade 7: the first session was attended by over 80. In these sessions pupils were taught the first-aid of what to do when someone collapses and how to tell if someone has just fainted or are having a cardiac arrest. The importance of calling for help was emphasised before being shown how to open an airway and how to perform 'Hands-Only' CPR. This is as effective as also providing breaths, at least in the early stages of resuscitation until help arrives and is a lot better than doing nothing. It overcomes the aversion that bystanders may have to providing the 'kiss of life'. Each of the participants had to undergo a hands-on training session with a pre & post-test. 

The students aim to continue and will 'own' this group as they enter grade 8 next academic year. We acknowledge the enthusiasm and dedication of the organising team in volunteering to invest their knowledge, time and developing skills to help progress AKU's mission.​
